title: Introducing Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, and Data
format_note: Three feature chapters (Whiteboards, Sheets, Data) each opened by a title card, then a staged demo, closed by a tagline and logo; music only.
one_thing: Claude now makes whiteboards, spreadsheets and dashboards that teammates edit alongside it, at the speed of thought.

transcript.voice_style: No voice. Captions covered 28% of runtime and local whisper only repeated one invented sentence, so it was discarded.
transcript.script_shape: All meaning is carried by on-screen type and typed prompts: three chapter titles, three typed or chat prompts, then a three-variant tagline and the logo.

good.observation: One long continuous take with one hard cut lets three features read as one connected product story rather than three ads.
Every chapter opens with the same card: line icon, light first line, bold product name in two lines of at most 3 words.
Typing the prompt on screen shows the user action and the result without any caption naming the problem.
good.evidence: f0006, f0007 prompt box; f0010 result

good.observation: One consistent invented story (GeeGolly pies, Day 1-12, 58,500 pre-orders) links whiteboard, sheet and dashboard with real-looking numbers.
good.evidence: f0010, f0016, f0019 share 58,500 and 6,500 figures

good.observation: Named coloured cursors (Claude, Mia, Rosa, Dev, June) make collaboration visible instead of stated, and the tagline reuses them.
The tagline is rebuilt live by a selection highlight swapping Plan, Share, Work, so the three chapters are summarised in one line.
Ground, type and accent stay constant for 58s, so the brand reads as calm and consistent.

weak.observation: Frame 0 is a near-empty frame with a small grey chip; the subject only builds after 1.3s.
Dashboard and sheet text is small, so only headline figures survive at phone width; the chart axes are about 10 px at 720p.
Closing wordmark holds about 1.8s and has no call to action, URL or availability line.
No cut is placed on a musical onset; pacing is by animation only.

rule_candidates.rule: A multi-feature launch can run as one continuous shot with chapter title cards; one hard cut in 58s still holds attention when an animated change lands every 2-3s.
Give every feature chapter the same title card template: icon above, light line then bold product name, centred, 6.7-10.8% of frame height.
Show collaboration with named, coloured cursors that touch the content, then reuse them in the tagline; keep each label visible at least 1s.
Prompt text is typed letter by letter on screen and held about 4s for 18 words, then the result is built by a cursor.
A tagline can be rebuilt by swapping its first word in place with a selection highlight, one swap about every 1.8s, so each variant lands once.
Open an animated launch with a chip and typing animation rather than a logo; frame 0 may be near-empty if the subject builds within 1.3s.
Keep one invented but consistent story and figures across all UI so the demo reads as a single business; use the same figures in headings and charts.
Close with silence under the wordmark: music stops about 1.2s before the end and the logo holds at least 2s.
